column1: # What Felix asks reality about itself.
# Felix may declare which question to ask. Felix may never author the answer.
# The members of every predicate below come back from the command; nothing in
# the engine can add one, and a row that returns nothing is never quietly read
# as a row with nothing to worry about.
# predicate
# A row with no witness can never report `empty` and always blocks as
# `unknown`, because a probe with nothing to check it against cannot tell an
# absent surface from a broken command — and every system that guesses there
# guesses "absent", which is the permissive direction. Every row here carries
# one, and each witness asks a different question from its probe: git's index
# versus the filesystem, the file's contents versus the file's existence. A
# witness that re-runs the probe agrees with it by construction and buys
# nothing.
# Two of these were written because of what this checkout could not answer on
# 2026-09-03. `hook_binding` reads the events the SHIPPED hooks.json binds,
# which is the fact deciding whether the floor runs at all — the night the
# marker bypass was found, nothing enumerated it. It reads them through
# bin/hooks-events, the same key scanner the first admitted obligation is
# judged by, and not through a grep for `"Event": [`: a blind-authored control
# moved a whole event entry one level down into another event's matcher group,
# every token intact and the hook never firing, and the grep counted it. A
# probe that shares a checker's shadow records the fact the checker misjudges.
# `test_assertion` grounds the
# `tests` capability, which this project declares and its own detector cannot
# see: felix_detect looks for tests/ at the repo root and this suite lives at
# engine/harness/tests, so the capability was declared, undetected, and
# unexamined by anything. A probe settles it; a filename match never could.
# Shrinking this file escapes to a person. It is in FELIX_ESCAPE_TABLES beside
# risk.tsv and deny.tsv, and it has its own row in risk.tsv with a verifier
# channel, because a probe removed is a fact nobody reads any more.
tracked_file
shell_entrypoint
hook_binding
governed_project
enforcing_table
test_assertion
ci_workflow
# The last two ask about this machine's felix, so each applies only where that
# felix exists: the cache holds a felix entry, the registry names a felix
# marketplace. marketplace_root used to apply wherever a registry could be
# read, so a machine that had registered any other marketplace read blind:
# every cloud session once a plugin was installed, and the clean runner of
# docs/handoff/0bm.md after the suite's own `claude` call wrote a registry.
# That is a machine without felix's marketplace, which is not-applicable, and
# `test -r` stays in front so a missing registry answers 1 and not grep's 2.
# deployed_engine enumerates one entry: the cache directory of the version
# main declares, down to the harness/ that felix_accepted_deploy_diff calls
# installed. That entry is the one the gate's `installed` check and the merge
# judge read. The row used to list every version the cache held, and the
# epoch hashes each row's member count, so pruning or installing any other
# version moved the topology and staled every green receipt on the machine
# while nothing the verdict rests on had changed. On 2026-10-08 a gate that
# took hours went stale two minutes after it passed, when the cache went from
# 40 versions to 39. Main's version is read the way the gate reads it,
# origin/main before main.
# The witness asks the registry rather than the filesystem. If the registry
# names main's version, the entry should be there, and a probe that found
# nothing is blind. If it names another version, main's engine is not
# deployed yet: the row reads empty, and the `installed` check names the
# remedy. A checkout with no main to read makes the witness exit 2, so the
# row is unknown and blocks, as the gate fails that checkout too.
deployed_engine
column4: b=origin/main; git rev-parse -q --verify "$b" >/dev/null || b=main; v="$(git show "$b:engine/.claude-plugin/plugin.json" | sed -n 's/.*"version"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -1)"; [ -n "$v" ] && ls -1d "$HOME/.claude/plugins/cache/felix/felix/$v/harness/"
